dedupe_keys.name: disruptionmap dependent infrastructure service disruption mapping

description: DISruptionMap (Dependent Infrastructure Service Disruption Mapping) is a method to assess how a large natural hazard disrupts critical infrastructure services directly and through cascades between dependent services. It was published in 2024 by Moritz Schneider, Lukas Halekotte, Andrea Mentges and Frank Fiedrich from the University of Wuppertal and the German Aerospace Center institute for the protection of terrestrial infrastructures. It combines spatial service models, which find where the hazard stops a service directly, with a service dependency model built from fault trees, which infers indirect disruptions; the fault tree approach cuts the information needed to set up dependencies, the main barrier for earlier spatial methods. The demonstration maps the impact of an extreme flood on health, transport and power services in Cologne, Germany. Coverage: method applicable to any area; one city case. Access: the arXiv paper describes the method; no code release was found. Licence and cost: the paper is CC BY 4.0 and free. Caveats: binary service states, dependencies elicited by the analyst, and one case study. It supports cascading failure and hazard exposure analysis for emergency planning, including road access to hospitals, and complements coupled network models such as InfraRisk in the catalogue.
